paragraphs: Mitzva al haadam lihyot measara rishonim bebet hakkeneset, veiqqar hammitzva sheyyishshaer sham lehitpallel sham, velo keotam sheyyihyu measara rishonim bebet hakkeneset veachar kak holekim lehitpallel bebet keneset acheret sheshsham enam measara harishonim vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot lerabbenu za"l, ukeshem shemmitzva lihyot measara rishonim beshacharit ken mitzva gam ken bemincha umaarib, vekol hammaqdim yoter hu qarob el haqqedushsha yoter usekaro yoter, ukeshem shemmitzva lihyot measara rishonim kak mitzva lehitakkeb ad shello yishshaaru asara bebet hakkeneset, umikkol shekken shetztzarik lehizzaher shello yetze rishon measara haacharonim sheharishon laasara haacharonim kesheyyatza mibbet hakkeneset hu haiqqar haggorem silluq or hashshekina mibbet hakkeneset, veayyen "eliyyahu raba" siman tz"g ot ' v"chesed laalapim" sham veod acharonim:

clarification.explanation: It is a mitzvah for a person to be among the first ten who arrive at the synagogue, but the essence of the mitzvah is that he also remain there to pray — not like one who arrives early only to be counted among the first ten and then goes to pray at a different synagogue, where he is no longer counted among the first ten. And just as there is a mitzvah in this regarding the morning prayer (Shacharit), so too there is a mitzvah regarding Minchah and Ma'ariv. And the earlier one arrives, the closer he draws to holiness, and the greater his reward. And just as there is a mitzvah to be among the first ten, so too there is a mitzvah to remain until only ten are left in the synagogue — and one must especially be careful not to be the first to leave from among the last ten who remain, for the first one of them to leave causes the removal of the light of the Shechinah from the synagogue.
takeaways: Try to arrive early at the synagogue and remain there to pray, not merely to be counted in the minyan and then leave.
Be careful not to be the first to leave when only ten worshippers remain at the end of the prayer.

paragraphs: Mitzva larutz kesheholek lebet hakkeneset, veken lekol debar mitzva, ak yaaseh beopen shello yaligu haroin alayv, ella yelek keish mahir bimlakto, veameru rabbotenu za"l al pasuq "melek asur barehatim" (shir hashshirim z, v) shehashshekina qeshura im yisrael baggalut bishbil shene ritzot sheratz abraham abinu alayv hashshalom bishbil mitzva diktib "vaymaher abraham haohela el sara" "veel habbaqar ratz abraham" (bereshit ych, v-z), veameru gam ken bazzohar haqqadosh kesheyyisrael ratzim lidbar mitzva, keneged zeh ratzim malake sangoriy umaqdimin lelammed zekut al yisrael, umihu lo yarutz ella ad petach bet hakkeneset, abal bebet hakkeneset atzmah asur larutz ella yelek beema veyira, ki hekal melek hakkabod hi vekannizkar b"chesed lealpayim":

clarification.explanation: It is a mitzvah to hurry and walk briskly on the way to the synagogue, and likewise for any matter of mitzvah, but in a manner that onlookers will not mock him — that is, he should walk like someone hurrying to something important, not run in a laughable way. Our Sages expounded on the verse "A king is held captive in the tresses" that the Shechinah is bound with the people of Israel in exile in the merit of the two runs that Abraham our father ran for the sake of a mitzvah (hurrying to prepare for his guests, and running to the cattle). And so it is explained in the holy Zohar, that when Israel run to perform a mitzvah, correspondingly the angels who are their advocates hurry to argue in their merit. But this law of running applies only until the entrance of the synagogue — within the synagogue itself it is forbidden to run; rather one should walk with awe and fear, for the synagogue is like the palace of a king.
takeaways: Hurry and hasten on the way to the synagogue and to any mitzvah, but in a dignified manner that will not provoke mockery.
Within the synagogue itself — walk slowly, with awe and fear, and do not run.

paragraphs: Hanniknas lebet hakkeneset yizzaher lehitakkeb meat bappetach qodem sheyyikkanes, uleharot atzmo yare vechared umizdazea likkanes behekal malko shel olam, veinyan zeh moil meod el hashshelemut shel haadam veel hahassaga, vezeh sod happasuq "umiqdashi tirau" (vayyiqra yt, l), gam zeh mah sheameru baggemara beinyan achitopel shellimmedo ledavid hammelek alayv hashshalom pasuq "bebet elohim nehallek beragesh" (tehillim nh, tv), sheramezu gam ken inyan beragesh sheyyitraggesh haadam veyizdazea beet kenisato bebet elohim shehu bet hakkeneset ad kan leshon rabbenu za"l beshaar hakkavvanot yeuyyan sham: ubeseper "keter malkut" ketibat yad katub bekol yom kesheyyikkanes lebet hakkeneset yaamod bepetach veyomar pasuq "vaani berob chasdeka veku'" (tehillim h, ch) veyikkanes, ukeshehu niknas veholek sham yomar achar happasuq hannizkar "Adonai tzebaot immanu misgab lanu elohe yaaqob sela" (sham mv, ch) vehu pasuq shel abraham abinu alayv hashshalom, veacharayv pasuq "Adonai tzebaot ashre adam boteach bak" (sham pd, yg) vehu shel yitzchaq abinu alayv hashshalom, veacharayv pasuq "Adonai hoshia hammelek yaanenu beyom qareenu" vehu shel yaaqob abinu alayv hashshalom, veim epshar leomeram kullam beamedo bappetach hinneh mah tob, veim lo epshar yomar shelosha pesuqim ellu keshehu niknas veholek ubechol lo yomar pasuq "vaani berob chasdeka" ella im ken lobesh tepillin, abal beshabbat veyom tob deen mannichin tepillin yomar pasuq "vaani berob chasdeka", vela baenan sheyyihyeh meuttap betzitzit deday bazeh betallit qatan shealayv:

clarification.explanation: One who enters the synagogue should pause briefly at the entrance before entering, and show himself fearful and trembling at entering the palace of the King of the world — and this greatly assists a person's spiritual perfection. This is the secret alluded to in the verse "and you shall fear My sanctuary," and likewise what our Sages related about Achitofel, who taught David the king from the verse "We walked to the house of God with tumult" — that one should be stirred and awestruck upon entering the synagogue. It is written in the book Keter Malchut that every day, when entering the synagogue, one should stand at the entrance and say the verse "But I, through the abundance of Your kindness, I will come into Your house" (only if he is wearing tefillin; but on Shabbat and Yom Tov, when there are no tefillin, he should say it always), and as he continues walking he should say three more verses — each belonging to one of the Patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. If it is possible to say them all while standing at the entrance — all the better; if not, he should say them while walking. There is no need to wrap oneself in a large tallit for this — the small tallit worn all day suffices.
takeaways: Pause for a moment at the entrance of the synagogue out of awe, before actually entering.
Say the special verses (of the Patriarchs) upon entering, according to the appropriate time and attire.

paragraphs: Yiqba maqom litpillato shello yeshannehu, velav davqa beqeba shel bet hakkeneset, ella gam bebet hakkeneset sheqqabua bah yiqba sham maqom, veken kesheyyitpallel bebeto lipraqim gam ken yiqba maqom lehitpallel bo bekol paam, veiqqar qebiut maqom hu bitpillat haamida:

clarification.explanation: One should establish for himself a fixed place for prayer and not change it. This applies not only to his regular synagogue, but also within that same synagogue — he should establish for himself a corner or particular spot. Likewise, if he sometimes prays at home, there too he should establish a fixed place for each time. The primary importance of establishing a fixed place applies especially to the Amidah prayer (the Shemoneh Esreh).
takeaways: Establish a fixed place for prayer for yourself and do not change it.
The main point is to establish a fixed place particularly for the Amidah prayer.

paragraphs: Asur lehitpallel beitztzabon, deim yitpallel beitztzabon en napsho yekola leqabbel or haelyon hannimshak alayv beet hattepilla, veraq bishat vidduy yitatztzeb al aonotayv, veqodem tepilla yeqabbel mitzvat veahabta lereaka kamoka, velaken im yesh adam miyyisrael betzara yitpallel alayv kol yom beperush, veal yede zeh tikkalel tepillato biklal tepillot kol yisrael vetaaseh peri lemala:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to pray out of sadness and gloom, for when a person is sad, his soul cannot absorb the supernal light that is drawn to him during prayer. The exception is the time of Vidui (confession of sins), when it is specifically fitting to feel sorrow over one's transgressions. Before prayer it is good to accept upon oneself the mitzvah of "Love your fellow as yourself," and therefore, if there is a Jew who is in distress, it is fitting to pray for him explicitly every day — and through this, one's personal prayer joins the collective prayers of all Israel and has a greater effect above.
takeaways: Pray out of joy and not out of sadness, except at the time of Vidui.
Before prayer, it is good to accept upon yourself love of Israel and to pray explicitly for someone who is in distress.

paragraphs: Apillu hazzemirot lo haya omer rabbenu haari"y za"l beqol ram, kede leharot haknaa, veraq beyom shabbat haya merim qolo binima meat yoter mimminhago bechol likbod shabbat, ukeshehaya qore ezeh pasuq mittana"k betok hattepillot dimyushshab haya qoreo bitamim shello, vehaya mazhir et rabbenu morenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l shello yaknis haetzba tok azenayv kede lenaqqotam mizzuhama mittechillat hattepilla dimyushshab ad gemar alenu leshabbeach, veal yede mitpachat let lan bah, katub beseper "keter malkut" ketibat yad kesheomer shelosha pesuqim "mi el kamoka vego'" shehem, y"g mikkaylan derachame yemanneh et hy"g hannizkarot beetzbeot hayyamin kederek sheosin baamirat achad asar sammane haqqetoret ad kan, veyapeh katab chada ki hamminyan yeravveh al chashibut umaala shel oto dabar vekevan dehem dabar shebbeminyan vadday tob limnotam beetzbaot leparsem minyanam, veod yoil zeh leorer hakkavvana balleb veken ani noheg:

clarification.explanation: Our teacher the Ari, of blessed memory, would not raise his voice even during the recitation of Pesukei D'Zimrah ("the Zemirot"), in order to show humility, and only on Shabbat would he raise his voice slightly in melody, in honor of Shabbat. When he read a verse from Tanach within the [seated portion of] prayer, he would read it with its cantillation marks. He would warn his disciple Rabbi Chaim Vital not to put his finger inside his ears to clean them, from the beginning of the seated prayer until the end of Aleinu L'Shabeach — but cleaning by means of a handkerchief is not a problem. It is written in the book Keter Malchut that when saying the three verses "Mi El Kamocha" (in which the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are alluded to), it is good to count the Thirteen Attributes on the fingers of the right hand, in the way one counts the eleven spices of the incense. The reason: counting expresses the importance and stature of the matter, and it also helps arouse concentration in the heart.
takeaways: One should pray quietly and humbly, not loudly, aside from a certain raising of the voice on Shabbat.
It is good to count the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy on the fingers of the right hand while saying "Mi El Kamocha," in order to arouse concentration.

paragraphs: Kesheyyaggia liqriat shema qodem parashat hattamid yizzaher lomar pesuqim shema yisrael ubaruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed bekavvana gedola kemo qeriat shema deyotzer, hen bisgirut enayv, veken bimsirat napsho betebat echad, ki zo hi chiyyub midderabbanan, vikavven leqayyem mitzvat qeriat shema midderabbanan veyesh bah tzorek gadol betiqqun hattepilla deen anachnu yekolim lehashlim tiqqun hannaaseh biqriat shema deyotzer ella betzerup qeriat shema zo, ak saggi lomar pasuq shema yisrael ubaruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed, veen omerim "veahabta vego'" vekannizkar beseper hakkavvanot: vehinneh bassiddurim katub qodem qeriat shema zo ashsherenu sheanachnu mashkimim umaaribim bebatte kenesiyyot bebatte midrashot umeyachadim shimka bekol yom veku', veen zo nuscha amittit demecheze kimshaqqer derob en mashkimim umaaribim bebatte kenesiyyot ubebatte midrashot, ak nuscha haiqqarit hu lehosip ot ka"p betebat sheanachnu velomar kesheanachnu mashkimin umaaribin, veli ana abada nireh deadip tepe lebilti nomar mashkimim umaaribim bebatte kenesiyyot ubebatte midrashot deqamme shemayya gallayya uma hekreach yesh lanu bidbarim ellu, ella yomar ashsherenu sheanachnu meyachadim shimka bekol yom veku' ken nireh li vehabbocher yibchar:

clarification.explanation: When one reaches the recitation of "Shema Yisrael" that precedes Parashat HaTamid (in the section of sacrifices), it should be said with great concentration, like the primary Shema recited in the blessings of Shema — with closing of the eyes and devotion of the soul on the word "Echad." This is a Shema of rabbinic origin, but it is greatly needed, since the rectification of the primary Shema (of the blessings of Yotzer) is incomplete without it. But here one says only the verse "Shema Yisrael..." and "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto L'Olam Va'ed," without continuing with "V'ahavta." Likewise, the text preceding this Shema should be corrected: the accepted text, "Happy are we, that we rise early and stay late at synagogues and study halls," is not accurate, because most people do not actually rise early and stay late at the synagogue. The essential text is to add the letter kaf and say "Happy are we, when we rise early and stay late at synagogues and study halls"; and in the opinion of the Ben Ish Chai, it is preferable to say only "Happy are we, that we unify Your Name every day," without the phrase about rising early and staying late — and let the one who chooses, choose.
takeaways: Say "Shema Yisrael... and Baruch Shem" with great concentration and devotion of soul, even though it is only a rabbinic obligation.

The essential text is to add the kaf and say "when we rise early and stay late"; and in the opinion of the Ben Ish Chai it is preferable to omit the phrase entirely and say only "we unify Your Name every day" — let the one who chooses, choose.

paragraphs: Parashat hattamid vehaqqetoret yomar bekavvana gedola derabbu mispar maaloteha, vehaqqeria bimqom haqraba veyimneh beetzbeotayv hassammanin shel hatztzori vehatztzipporen veku', vekatabti besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" besiyyata dishmayya dehamminyan moreh al chashibut umaala, dilhaki qayma lan kol dabar shebbeminyan apillu beelep lo batel veod bazeh titorer hakkavvana yoter, veod ikka tama beminyan haetzbaot deap al gab diqriatenu hi haola bimqom haqtara, im kol zeh lerob yaqar tiperet hammitzva hazzot netzarep im sicha siptotenu ezeh tenua shel maaseh, velaken nimneh beetzbaot kede laasot qetzat peulla beyadenu bedabar zeh veaz yitztarepu haddibbur vehammaaseh keillu hiqtarnu mammash, velaken nireh li detob lemannot beetzbeot hayyamin davqa udelo kemo shekkatebu dimanneh bishtehen kede lizkot shette yadot keechad, chada demaaseh hayyamin mesuggelet yoter bekol maqom, veod ki hakkohen hammaqtir bebet hammiqdash haya maqtir beyamin, veod katabti sham taam limnot haetzbaot ki haechad asar sammanim hem berurim shel shiba melakim shehem sheba sepirot: chesed gebura tiperet netzach hod yesod malkut, veyadua dechamesh etzbaot hem chesed gebura tiperet venetzach vehod kemo shekkatub beshaar hakkavvanot bidrush hatztzitzit, venimtza rob sheba sepirot nirmazim beetzbeot hayyad laken moneh bahem: ubeseper "keter malkut" ketibat yad ita degam achad asar sammanim shennirmezu bammiqra shel "qach leka sammim vego'" gam ken yemanneh otam beetzbaot, dehaynu "qach leka sammim" yemanneh shettayim, ub"natap ushechelet vechelbena" yemanneh od shalosh, ub"sammim" hashshenit yimneh od chamesh, ub"lebona zaka" yemanneh od achat, veyapeh katab bazeh umistabber tameh veken ani noheg:

clarification.explanation: One should say Parashat HaTamid and the Ketoret with great concentration, for it has many virtues — the reading stands in place of the actual offering. When reciting the spices of the incense (the tzori, the tziporen, etc.), it is good to count them on the fingers. The reason: counting expresses the importance of the matter (following the principle that anything counted is never nullified even when among a thousand), and it also further arouses concentration. Furthermore, even though our reading stands in place of the actual burning of the incense, we nevertheless wish to join an actual action (the movement of the fingers) to the speech, as if we had truly burned the incense. One should count specifically with the right hand (and not with both hands, as others have written), because the action of the right hand is more effective everywhere, and also because the Kohen in the Temple would burn the incense with his right hand. There is also a further reason based on the Kabbalah: the eleven spices of the incense are the rectification of the seven Sefirot (Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malchut), and the five fingers of the hand allude to five of the Sefirot (Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod), and therefore they are counted on the fingers. The book Keter Malchut also brings a way to count on the fingers the eleven spices alluded to in the verse: for "Take for yourself spices" one counts two; for "nataf, ushechelet, v'chelbanah" three more; for "samim" the second time, five more; and for "levonah zakah" one more — and so the Ben Ish Chai practiced in fact.
takeaways: Say Parashat HaKetoret with great concentration, and count the spices specifically on the fingers of the right hand.
The counting expresses importance, arouses concentration, and joins actual deed to speech.

paragraphs: Yesh medaqdeqin lomar abbayye hu hava mesadder, kede shello tidbaq yo"d shel abbayye im hava deaz nireh keqore hashshem kiktabo veken rauy laasot, upesuqe anna bekoach yomar kol shette tebot beyachad anna bekoach veyapsiq, veachar kak gedullat yemineka veyapsiq, veken al zeh hadderek vikavven berashe hattebot bishmot haqqodesh kannizkar bassiddurim, vekatab "minchat aharon" kelal y' ot q' vezeh leshono: veah"shiyyure keneset haggedola" katab laamod beet omero ana bekoach, ukebar katabti leel deen chiyyub laamod al raglayv ella bemaqom sheanachnu asuqim bishlosha rishonot veim ken en laamod kesheomer ana bekoach deinyan zeh eno lo beketer velo beabba veimma ad kan leshono veyapeh katab, veshaalti al minhag hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz veameru sheen minhagam laamod:

clarification.explanation: Some are precise to say "Abaye hu havah mesader" — adding the word "hu" — so that the yud of "Abaye" will not attach to "havah," which would then appear as if one is pronouncing the [Divine] Name as it is written — and so it is fitting to do. And in the verses of "Ana B'Choach," one should say every two words together and pause: "Ana B'Choach" — pause; "Gedulat Yeminecha" — pause; and so on in this manner, with intent on the acrostics of the holy Names (as found in the prayer books). Minchat Aharon writes that Shiyurei Kenesset HaGedolah wrote to stand while saying "Ana B'Choach"; but there is no obligation to stand except in a place where one is engaged with the first three Sefirot, and "Ana B'Choach" is neither in Keter nor in Abba and Imma — so there is no need to stand for it. And the Ben Ish Chai inquired about the custom of Beit El, and was told that it is not their custom to stand.
takeaways: One says "Abaye hu havah mesader" — with the word "hu" — so that the yud of "Abaye" will not attach to "havah" and appear as pronouncing the [Divine] Name as written.
"Ana B'Choach" — every two words together with a pause, with intent on the acrostics of the holy Names; there is no obligation to stand for it (and so is the custom of Beit El).

paragraphs: Barayta derabbi yishmael yesh bah sodot gedolim ubesiddur rabbenu harasha"sh mesuddarim lenakon, al ken tzarik leomerah benachat umittun, ubeseper "keter malkut" ketibat yad gam al barayta zo katab: tob limnot shelosh esreh middot shebbah beetzbaot vetamo venimmuqo immo, vekatub beshaar hakkavvanot lomar "veken" bepata"ch yeuyyan sham, veyesh maqshim vahalo matzinu "ken" btzr"y bimlakim ' siman z' (pasuq kt) "veal hashlabbim ken mimmaal", veod sham (pasuq lo) "agol maaseh ken" kol zeh hu milleshon "oti heshib al kanni" (bereshit m yg), veen zo qusheya kelal dein haki name yesh "ken" btzr"y shehu mimmashmaut zo ak "ken" bepata"ch hu lashon meborar yoter bemashmaut zo, veod nireh vadday sheyyesh al pi hassod taam etzel rabbenu haari"y za"l shetztzarik lomar ken bepata"ch:

clarification.explanation: The Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael (recited in the morning prayer) contains great secrets, and therefore one should recite it calmly and deliberately. Here too it is good to count on the fingers the Thirteen Principles by which the Torah is expounded. There is a grammatical discussion regarding the text: how should the word "ken" within the Baraita be vocalized — with a patach or a tzeirei? Some raised the difficulty that elsewhere in Scripture the word "ken" appears with a tzeirei in a similar sense, but it is explained that although indeed "ken" with a tzeirei exists with this meaning, nevertheless "ken" with a patach expresses the meaning more clearly, and moreover there is a reason for this according to the Kabbalah in the words of the Ari, of blessed memory.
takeaways: Recite the Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael slowly and with concentration; it is good to count the Thirteen Principles on the fingers.
Vocalize the word "ken" within the Baraita with a patach, not a tzeirei.

paragraphs: Tob lismok amirat pesuqim shel hodu leparashat hattamid veezehu meqoman bekol mah deepshar yaan ki betamid shel shachar hayu omerim mi"hodu lah'" ad "ubinbie al trv", ubetamid shel ben haarbayim hayu omerim mi"shiru laAdonai kol haaretz" ad "vehallel lah'", veal pi hassod yesh taam bipsuqim ellu kede lehaprid haqqelippot meal haqqedushsha, umi sheyyesh lo ezeh sibba shello yukal lehaqdim labo lebet hakkeneset lehatchil hattepilla mipparashat haaqeda im hatztzibbur shehu mukrach lehatchil bebeto lebaddo ad "Adonai melek", yachazor veyomar paam shenit pesuqim shel hodu kede lehasmikam lizmirot al pi hassod, ubebeto gam ken mukrach haya leomeram kede lesomekam im parashat hattamid, ushear qarebbanot, vehinneh noda minhag haashkenazzim lomar pesuqim shel hodu achar baruk sheamar, uminhag hasseparaddim qodem ushene minhagim ellu yesh bahem taam al pi hassod, veyadua mah shekkatub beseper hakkavvanot derabbenu haari"y za"l haya oseh bedabar zeh keminhag hasseparaddim upasuq "hodu laAdonai ki tob ki leolam chasdo" asher betok pesuqe hodu hannizkarim en kopelin oto, ella omerim oto paam achat, vegam hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz en minhagam likpol:

clarification.explanation: It is good, when possible, to join the recitation of the verses of "Hodu" directly to Parashat HaTamid and "Eizehu Mekoman" without a break, because in the Temple, at the morning Tamid offering they would say a certain passage of verses, and at the afternoon Tamid offering — a different passage. There is also a reason for this according to the Kabbalah: to separate the kelipot from holiness. One who is delayed and arrives at the synagogue after the congregation has already begun the prayer from Parashat Ha'Akeidah, and is forced to begin alone at home until "HaShem Melech," must go back and say the verses of "Hodu" again (a second time) in order to properly join them to the Zemirot, since he should have said them at home as well, to join them to Parashat HaTamid. There is a difference in custom: the Ashkenazim say the verses of "Hodu" after "Baruch SheAmar," while the Sephardim say them before it, and both customs have a reason according to the Kabbalah; but the Ari, of blessed memory, followed the Sephardic custom (before "Baruch SheAmar"). Likewise, the verse "Hodu LaShem ki tov ki l'olam chasdo," within the verses of "Hodu," should not be doubled — it is said only once, and this is also the practice in Beit El.
takeaways: Join the verses of "Hodu" to Parashat HaTamid as much as possible, without a break between them.
One who prayed alone at home and did not manage to join them properly should go back and say the verses of "Hodu" again with the congregation.
Do not double the verse "Hodu LaShem ki tov ki l'olam chasdo" — say it only once.

paragraphs: Yizzaher kol adam lomar qodem parashat haaqeda nosach zeh, ribbon alema yehe raava qammak lemehab lan chela leittara biqarak, ulemebad reuteka, ulesidra kolla kidqa yaut, veap al gab deli anan yadein lishvaa reuta velabo letaqena kolla, yehe raava qammak detitrai bemillin vetzilluta dilan, letaqena tiqquna dilella deqa yaut, ulehavu hayyakelin illain, veruchin illain ayeli hekela behekela, verucha berucha, kad dimchabberan beduktayhu kidqa chaze, sheyapa beshiypepa, veishtallimu da bada, veityachadu da bada ad innun chad, venaharin da bada, ukedin nishmeta illaa dekolla ateya milleela venaher lon, velehve nehirin kullehu butzinin beshelleyammo kidqa chaze, ad dehahu nehora illaa attaar, vekolla aayel legabbe qodesh qodashim, veitbarka veitmalliya kebira dameyan nabein vela paseqin, vekullehu mitbarkan leella utetta, vehahu dela ityeyda vela ael bechushbana reuta dela atpes lealemin besim lego lego begavvayhu vela ityadda hahu reuta vela atpes lemanda, ukedin kelo reuta chada ad en sop vekolla yehu beshelleyammo milletatta umiggo lego ad deitabid kelo chad, veitmeliat kelo veashshetalim kelo veetnaher veetbassem kelo kidqa yaut: ribbon alema yehe reutek im ammeka yisrael leolam, upurqan yemineka achzay leammeka bebet miqdasheka, uleamtoye lana mittub nehorak, uleqabbel tzelotana berachame, yehe raava qammak deteheve said usemik lan, denema milin beorach mishor, betiqquna dilella, betiqqunin demalka qaddisha umatronita qaddisha, ulemebad yechuda shelim, leashlepa lehahi neshama dekol chayye middarga ledarga ad sopa dekol dargin, begin deyeheve hahi nishmeta mishtakcha bakkele umitpashshet bakkele, deha illa vetatta taleyin behay nishmeta umitqayyeme bah ad kan, ubazeh hannussach sheomer haadam bekol yom qodem tepilla yihyeh mutztzal millatuta derabbi shimon bar yochay delayet baiddera raba dap qm" ammud b (ch"g qamma, b), vah' lo yimna tob laholekim betamim.

clarification.explanation: Before Parashat Ha'Akeidah one should recite the Aramaic text "Ribbono Shel Olam" ("Master of the Universe") found in the holy Zohar, in which a person asks the Holy One, blessed be He, for strength to arouse His honor and to do His will, and asks that the prayer help to rectify and unify the supernal worlds — that all the "chambers" and "spirits" join together properly, until they become fully united and the supernal light shines upon them, and everything ascends to the Holy of Holies and is blessed and filled like a wellspring that never ceases. Further in the text, one asks that God's will be with the people of Israel forever, that the redemption be revealed, that one's prayer be accepted in mercy, and that one merit to speak the words in a straight path, in accordance with the supernal rectification and complete union. One who recites this text every day before prayer is spared from the curse that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai pronounced in the Idra Rabba.
takeaways: It is good to say every day, before prayer, the text of "Ribbono Shel Olam" brought in the Zohar.
Reciting the text protects from the curse of Rashbi in the Idra Rabba, and assists supernal rectification.

paragraphs: Od matzati katub mah tob umah naim sheyyomar haadam bekol yom achar tiqqun chatzot dehaynu achar sheyyomar petichat eliyyahu zakur lattob, leshon rabbi shimon bar yochay bazzohar haqqadosh parashat noach dap s"h ammud  ubeparashat pequde dap rs"ch ammud b amar rabbi shimon aremit yeday bitzlotin leella, dekad reuta illaa leella veku' veku', ad veal da kullam qaem zakkaa chulaqehon detzaddiqayya bealema din ubealema deate, veim lo haya yakol leomeram achar chatzot layla yomar otam beshacharit qodem tepilla, veken yaaseh gam beshabbatot veyamim tobim ki debarim ellu hem amuqqim meod meod, vehammebin sodan shel debarim ellu yeda kamma toelet naasa baamiratam letiqqun oto hayyom ben bepartzup hayyamim ben bepartzup hazzemannim:

clarification.explanation: I found it written that it is fitting to say every day, after Tikkun Chatzot (after reciting "Eliyahu Zachur LaTov"), a passage from the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in the holy Zohar (in Parashat Noach and Parashat Pekudei) beginning with "Arimit yedai b'tzalotin l'eila" ["I raised my hands in prayer above"], which describes how prayer performed out of supernal will has an effect above, and concludes with "happy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the World to Come." One who did not manage to say it after midnight should say it in the morning before prayer. And one should do likewise also on Shabbatot and Yamim Tovim, for these matters are very profound, and one who understands their secret knows how much great benefit there is in reciting them for the rectification of that day.
takeaways: Say the passage "Arimit Yedai" from the Zohar after Tikkun Chatzot, or in the morning before prayer if one did not manage to.
Do likewise also on Shabbatot and Yamim Tovim, because of the depth of the secret of these matters.

paragraphs: Inyan gadol venora veetza toba viqara, gilla lanu rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar rucha haqqodesh yichud k", vehu: rauy laadam tamid lekavven ulehaarik et atzmo keillu hu mador vekisse el haatzilut haqqadosh, ubiprat bizman shehaadam mitpallel hu yoter rauy umukrach sheyyekavven bekak, vead yede ken tishreh vetachul alayv qedushsha elyona.

Vezehu mah sheyyekavven: techilla yachshob shehu mekin gulgolet rosho (shehu sod keter) lihyot kisse el shem havaya"h beniqqud qm"tz kullah, veod mekin mocha chakema shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud pat"ch, umekin mocha bina shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud tzere, umekin ayin yamin shebbo lihyot kisse el chamishsha hvyv"t beniqqud tzere, umekin ayin yamin shebbo lihyot kisse el chamishsha hvyv"t shehem mispar ayi"n umekin ayin semol shebbo lihyot kisse lachamishsha hvyv"t shehem mispar ayi"n, veyakin ozen yamin shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h bemillua kazeh yu"d h"y va"v h"h shehu mispar "ozen", veyakin ozen semol shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h bemilluy zeh yu"d h"y va"v h"h shehu mispar "ozen", veyakin nechir yamin dechotem shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h bemilluy zeh yu"d h"y va"v h"y sheoleh mispar "chotem", veyakin nechir semol dechotem shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h bemilluy zeh yu"d h"y va"v h"y sheoleh mispar "chotem", veyakin peh shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h bemilluy zeh yu"d h"y va"v h"y, vk"b otiyyot shel chamishsha motzaot happeh (shehem chh" gyk"q dtln"t zsshr"tz bvm"p) sheoleh sak hakkol poh, veyakin zeroa yamin shebbo kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud sgv"l, veyakin zeroa semol shebbo kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud shb", veyakin gupo kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud chvl"m, veyakin yerek yamin shebbo kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud chyr"q, veyakin yerek semol shebbo kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud qibbutz, veyakin habberit shehu yesod shebbo kisse leshem hvy"h beniqqud shvr"q beva"v, veyakin haatara shebbo lihyot kisse leshem hvy"h bilti naqud ad kan debarayv. umatzati katub kesheyyekavven bhvy"h zo bilti naqud tzarik letzayyer betok ot Adonai acharona shem dn"y ad kan debarayv vehu kaptor vaperach:

clarification.explanation: The Ari, of blessed memory, revealed a great and sublime matter: it is fitting for a person, especially during prayer, to intend and regard himself as though his entire body were a "dwelling and throne" for the holy divine light (Atzilut), and through this a supernal holiness rests upon him. The detailed intention brought in Sha'ar Ruach HaKodesh is as follows: every part of the body — the skull, the brain of Chochmah, the brain of Binah, the two eyes, the two ears, the two nostrils of the nose, the mouth, the two arms, the body itself, the two thighs, the covenant of circumcision, and the crown — becomes, through this intention, a "throne" for the Name HaVaYaH, with a particular vocalization or spelling suited to it (for example kamatz, patach, tzeirei, segol, shva, cholam, chirik, kubutz, shuruk, and so on), where each vocalization has a numerical value matching the name of that limb (for example, a certain vocalization equals in gematria the word "ozen" [ear], another equals "chotem" [nose], and so on). In other words, this is a complete map of the body, in which each part is devoted to a particular aspect of the Holy Name, like a precise "kaftor vaferach." And they further added: when one intends the Name HaVaYaH corresponding to the crown (which has no vocalization at all), one should picture in one's mind, within the final letter Hei, the Name Adonai — an additional detail in the secret of that intention.
takeaways: During prayer it is good to intend and picture the parts of the body as a "throne" for the holy Name of God, according to the intention of the Ari, of blessed memory.
One who wishes to practice this should first write out for himself the list of the Names and their vocalizations, and after becoming accustomed to it, will be able to intend them by heart.
In the intention for the crown (the unvocalized Name HaVaYaH), one should picture within the final letter Hei the Name Adonai.

paragraphs: Veda ki besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l hosip od kavvanot beseder hammerkaba hannizkar lekavven bedaat elyon ubedaat tachton, veod bahakanat happeh hosip lekavven beshem ehyeh, vaani lo zakarti poh ella mah shemmeporash lehedya bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar rucha haqqodesh. vezeh shekkatabnu kol adam yakol lekavven bazeh. utechilla yirshom hashshemot im niqqudehem basseper, veachar sheyyargil bahem az yukal lekavven hakkol beal peh velo yitztarek lirot et harashum biktab. veal ken tob sheyyargil laasot kavvanot hannizkar kol layla al mittato qodem sheyyiqra qeriat shema al hammitta. gam nakon lomar achar kak tv"b peamim pasuq "enay tamid el Adonai ki hu yotzi mereshet raglay" (tehillim kh, tv), ubekol paam yekavven beshem hvy"h kavvana achat mishsheba esreh kavvanot hannizkarot ki hakkavvanot shel hakkavvanot hannizkarot hem misseper tob, umaskil al dabar yimtza tob:

clarification.explanation: In the prayer book of the Rashash (Rabbi Shalom Sharabi) further intentions were added to the order of the "Merkavah" mentioned in the previous halachah — an intention also in "Da'at Elyon" and "Da'at Tachton," and in the intention of the mouth they added to intend also with the Name "Ehyeh." Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that he has brought here only what is explicitly stated in the words of the Ari himself, and that any person can intend this. At first it is worthwhile to write down for oneself the Names with their vocalization in writing, and after becoming accustomed to them, one will be able to intend it all by heart without needing to look at the list. It is good to practice these intentions every night on one's bed, before the Shema recited upon retiring. It is also good to say afterward the verse "My eyes are always toward the Lord, for He shall bring my feet out of the net" seventeen (17) times, intending each time with the Name HaVaYaH a different one of the seventeen intentions mentioned — since the number of the intentions equals [the numerical value of] "tov" [good].
takeaways: One may begin practicing the intentions of the "Merkavah" in writing, and later intend them by heart.
It is good to practice this every night on one's bed before the Shema recited upon retiring, and to say the verse "My eyes are always" seventeen times.
